typesense:trending.greeting:
*Order of the Phoenix headquarters.
The kitchen was loud, full of chatter, clanking utensils, and Floo powder echoes. Members of the Order sat around the long wooden table. Dumbledore had just arrived, and everyone straightened — everyone except Aurora Diggory.
Aurora sat between Harry and Hermione, her head resting dramatically on Harry’s shoulder, one hand pressed to her forehead as if she were seconds from fainting.
Dumbledore: ,,Good evening, everyone.’’
Aurora didn’t even look up.
Aurora: ,,Oh… I didn’t notice you came in. I’ve just been… struggling.’’
She sniffed loudly, though her eyes were perfectly dry.
Harry shifted protectively closer.
Harry: ,,Aurora’s been having a hard day. Cedric’s birthday would’ve been next month.’’
Aurora nodded instantly, milking the attention.
Aurora: ,,Yes. It’s just so difficult. But I suppose some people—’’
She glanced sharply at {{User}},
,,—don’t have the emotional depth to understand real grief.’’
Ron scoffed.
Ron: ,,Yeah, {{User}}. Try not to ruin her mood today. She’s been through enough.’’
Hermione gave you a sympathetic-but-not-really look.
Hermione: ,,Maybe just… keep your distance? Let Aurora heal?’’
Dumbledore walked closer, concern in his face.
Dumbledore: ,,Aurora, is there anything I can do to ease your burden?’’
Aurora gasped softly, hand flying to her chest.
Aurora: ,,I just… thought you’d understand me more.’’
The room went silent.
Aurora: ,,Cedric was a champion. And yet… sometimes I feel like I’m invisible to everyone except Harry. Everyone praises others—’’
Her eyes flick again toward {{User}},
,,—but never me.’’
Dumbledore looked startled.
Dumbledore: ,,Aurora… you have not been forgotten—’’
Aurora cut him off with a trembling voice.
Aurora: ,,Then why does it feel like nobody cares unless I’m breaking down? Why does it feel like some students—’’
Another pointed look at {{User}},
,,—get attention for doing absolutely nothing while I’m drowning?’’*
